newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs await BOJ branch managers' meeting in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: JGBs await BOJ branch managers' meeting in Tokyo.

text.p: The Japanese government bond (JGB) market is waiting for the two-day meeting of Bank of Japan (BOJ) branch managers starting on Monday, traders said.
The managers may present a slightly optimistic view of the economy, a view which would be theoretically bearish for bonds.

However, traders said that even if they turn slightly optimistic over the economy, the bad loan problems afflicting the Japanese financial system are likely to keep the BOJ from moving towards a credit tightening. The market is keen on the bad loan problems at general contractors and the burden on the small banks which have made loans to them.
The upside of the JGB market is likely to be capped by a slew of corporate bond issues this week.
Hitachi Transport Co, Aoki International Co, Oki Electric, JR East all plan bond issues this week, traders said.
The market is also watching closely if nine life insurers which have made subordinated loans to Sanyo Securities Co Ltd will extend their repayment date.

These loans have already been extended by six months in January and the insurers are unlikely to extend them again. Sanyo's capital ratio is likely to worsen significantly should it fail to get fresh loans.-- Yoshiko Mori, Tokyo Treasury Desk
